Question B-007-004-008.

Why the correct answer is right: Selective fading happens when components of the same transmission arrive with different phases at the receiving station. Parts of a wider signal can then be strengthened or weakened unequally.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Small changes in directional antenna heading at the receiving station": Turning an antenna may change level, but it is not the propagation cause of selective fading within the signal.
- sourceIndex 2: "Time differences between the receiving and transmitting stations": Clock differences between stations are irrelevant; the issue is path delay and phase among received components.
- sourceIndex 3: "Large changes in the height of the ionosphere at the receiving station ordinarily occurring shortly before sunrise and sunset": Sunrise and sunset layer changes can alter propagation, but selective fading is caused by multipath phase differences at the receiver.
